verses.text: So what’s the story with Abraham, our ancestor? What did he get by relying on human effort?
If Abraham got right with God by his own work, he could flex—but not in front of God.
Scripture says, “Abraham trusted God, and God counted that trust as righteousness.”
When you work, your paycheck isn’t a gift; it’s what you’re owed.
But when you stop trying to earn it and trust the God who makes the ungodly right, that faith gets counted as righteousness.
David says the same about the person God calls righteous without a work-credit score:
“Blessed are the people whose wrongs are forgiven and whose sins are covered.
“Blessed is the person whose sin the Lord will never count against them.”
So is this blessing only for the circumcised, or is it for the uncircumcised too? We’ve said God counted Abraham’s faith as righteousness.
When did God count it—after circumcision, or before? Before, not after.

Abraham received circumcision as a sign and seal of the righteousness he already had by faith while uncircumcised. That made him father to everyone who believes without the mark, so they too can be counted righteous.
He’s also father to the circumcised who don’t just have the mark but follow the same faith our father Abraham had before he was circumcised.
God’s promise to Abraham and his descendants—that he’d inherit the world—came through faith’s righteousness, not through the Law.
If the Law’s people are the heirs, faith gets emptied out and the promise is canceled.
The Law brings judgment. Where there’s no law, there can’t be a lawbreaking charge either.
That’s why the promise runs on faith: it comes by grace and stays solid for all Abraham’s descendants—not only those under the Law, but everyone who shares Abraham’s faith. He’s the father of us all.
Just as Scripture says, “I’ve made you father of many nations.” Abraham stood before the God he trusted—the God who gives life to the dead and calls what doesn’t exist into being.
When hope looked gone, Abraham still held on to hope and trusted God. That’s how he became father of many nations, just as God promised: “Your descendants will be that many.” 🌟
His faith didn’t fold when he looked at his own worn-out body—he was about a hundred—or at Sarah’s womb, which couldn’t have children.
He didn’t let unbelief knock him off God’s promise. His faith got stronger, and he gave glory to God.
He was fully convinced God had the power to do exactly what he promised. 🙏
That’s why God counted Abraham’s faith as righteousness.
And this wasn’t written down for Abraham alone.
It was written for us too. God will count faith as righteousness for us who trust the God who raised Jesus our Lord from the dead.
Jesus was handed over because of our wrongs and raised so we could be made right with God.
